mainTopic: Buying three trees in another's field: the land around them, the picking space, and how far apart the trees may be
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ruling that a buyer of three trees in someone else's field owns room around them for a fig-picker and his basket. רבי אלעזר objects: if the buyer gets no path, because his plot counts as separate land, why should he get picking space? From this, רבי זירא learns that a buyer of only two trees does get a path. רב נחמן בר יצחק asks whether רבי אלעזר is going against his teacher שמואל, who rules like רבי עקיבא that a seller sells generously. רבא answers that the משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא, but רב נחמן בר יצחק pushes back on רבא's proof. A ברייתא then supports the picking-space rule. אביי and רב יוסף discuss who may plant that space, and a ברייתא backs אביי that no one may. Finally, the גמרא asks how far apart the three trees may be. Two reports of שמואל give 4–8 or 8–16 אמות. אביי brings a משנה about a vineyard planted 16 by 16 to support the larger range, and רב יוסף begins to reply with a real case that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The buyer gets room for a fig-picker and his basket
steps.stepSummary: The tail of a ruling: the buyer of the trees acquires space around them big enough for a fig-picker and his basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: He acquires an area the size of a fig-picker and his basket.
steps.whatsHappening: We start in the middle of a ruling given just before. The buyer of the trees owns enough ground around them for a fig-picker to stand with his basket.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ground under and around three trees belongs to the buyer. This line tells us how much: enough room to pick the fruit. The next step will challenge exactly this point.

keyTerms.meaning: A fig-picker, the person who gathers the fruit
The full size of; as much as

phrases.english: As much as a fig-picker and his basket.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a ruling that began just before; the buyer owns this much space next to his trees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ruling begun earlier on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The buyer of three trees owns space around them big enough for a fig-picker and his basket.

steps.title: No path, so why picking space?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר objects: if the buyer has no path because his land is a separate piece of land, how can he have a right to picking space?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר objects: Now, if he has no path, does he have room for a fig-picker and his basket? He has no path because it counts as a different piece of land. So how does he have room for a picker and basket?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר attacks the ruling from step 1. He says it does not fit with the rule that the buyer has no path to his trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer gets no path because his trees stand on their own piece of land, cut off from the seller's field. If the seller gave him that little, he surely did not give him extra space for picking. Giving him picking space seems more generous than giving him a path.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenges it; he raises a strong objection
A path, a right to walk through the field

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar objects to it:
Now, he has no path,
yet he has room for a fig-picker and his basket?!

phrases.aramaic: דֶּרֶךְ אֵין לוֹ – דְּאַרְעָא אַחֲרִיתִי הִיא;
phrases.english: He has no path, because it is a different piece of land;
phrases.notes: His land around the trees counts as its own plot, so he has no right to walk through the seller's field.

phrases.english: so does he have room for a picker and his basket?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the picking-space ruling of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the buyer gets space for a fig-picker and his basket.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the buyer has no path, because his land is separate, he should not get the extra picking space either; the two rules do not fit together.

steps.title: With two trees, the buyer does get a path
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא learns from רבי אלעזר's objection that only with three trees is there no path; with two trees the buyer does have a path.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: From our teacher's words we learn that only with three trees does he have no path. But with two trees he does have a path, because he can say to the owner: My trees stand on your land.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא draws a new rule out of רבי אלעזר's objection. With two trees, the buyer gets a path.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said there is no path because it is a different piece of land. That only happens with three trees, when the buyer owns the ground. With two trees the buyer owns no ground, so his trees stand on the seller's land, and he may walk there to reach them.

keyTerms.meaning: Our teacher (רבי זירא means רבי אלעזר)

steps.whatToRemember: Three trees: the buyer owns the ground but gets no path. Two trees: he owns no ground, but he can walk to his trees, since they stand on the seller's land.
steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards that the buyer of fewer trees gets a path. With two trees he owns no land at all, so his trees are guests on the seller's land, and that gives him the right to reach them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
From the words of our teacher we learn,
phrases.notes: "Our teacher" is רבי אלעזר, and his "words" are the objection we just saw.

phrases.english: that it is with three trees that he has no path,
but with two, he does have a path,
since he says to him: They stand on your land.
phrases.notes: The buyer is telling the field owner that the trees stand on the owner's land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side rule from the reasoning inside רבי אלעזר's objection.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A buyer of two trees in someone else's field has a path to them, because his trees stand on the seller's land.

steps.title: Does רבי אלעזר disagree with his teacher שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רבא: שמואל rules like רבי עקיבא that a seller sells generously, so the buyer should get a path. Does רבי אלעזר reject his teacher's view?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: Shall we say that רבי אלעזר does not accept the view of שמואל, his teacher? שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא, who said that a seller sells generously.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק questions the base of רבי אלעזר's objection. He asks whether it goes against שמואל's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's objection assumes the buyer gets no path. But רבי עקיבא holds that a seller sells generously, so a path should be included. שמואל, רבי אלעזר's own teacher, rules like רבי עקיבא, so it seems strange for רבי אלעזר to assume otherwise.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (often opens a challenge)
He does not hold; he does not accept
A seller sells generously, giving the buyer the benefit of the doubt

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:
Shall we say that Rabbi Elazar does not accept
the view of Shmuel, his teacher?
For Shmuel said: The halacha follows Rabbi Akiva,
who said: A seller sells generously?
phrases.notes: If the seller is generous, he would include a path to the trees he sold.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לֵית לֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל רַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי אלעזר's objection in step 2 and questions what it assumes.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's assumption that the buyer has no path.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to רבי עקיבא a seller sells generously, so the buyer gets a path. שמואל, רבי אלעזר's teacher, rules like רבי עקיבא, so רבי אלעזר seems to go against his teacher.

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the משנה cannot be explained according to רבי עקיבא, so רבי אלעזר's objection works within the משנה's own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The משנה cannot be explained according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends רבי אלעזר. The objection was based on the משנה, and the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר may personally hold like רבי עקיבא, as שמואל rules. But the משנה that says the buyer has no path must follow the view that a seller does not sell generously. רבי אלעזר is only asking how the ruling in step 1 fits with that משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot be explained as; it cannot be set up as

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר did not reject שמואל. His question was about how to read the משנה, and the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is the one answering.

phrases.english: The mishnah cannot be explained according to Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separates the משנה's view from רבי אלעזר's personal view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's objection seemed to reject שמואל's ruling like רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה must follow the view that a seller does not sell generously, so רבי אלעזר's objection is about the משנה, not his own opinion.

steps.title: רבא's proof that the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his claim from the משנה's ruling that if the trees grow, the field owner may trim them. רבי עקיבא, who says a seller sells generously, would not allow that.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know? From the משנה's teaching: 'If the trees grew, he may trim them.' If you think this is רבי עקיבא's view, why may he trim them? Doesn't רבי עקיבא say a seller sells generously?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his answer from step 5 by showing a line in the משנה that clashes with רבי עקיבא's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the land owner cut back branches that grow into his field. If the seller were generous, as רבי עקיבא holds, he would let the buyer's trees spread. So the משנה must follow the רבנן, and רבי אלעזר's objection fits the משנה's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? (asking for the source of a claim)
He may trim / cut back the branches
It enters your mind (if you were to think)
With a generous eye, giving freely

phrases.english: From where do we know? From the fact that it teaches:
phrases.notes: This is רבא proving what he said in the last step: that the משנה can't follow רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: If they grew, he may trim them,
phrases.notes: 'They' are the three trees. 'He' is the owner of the field, cutting branches that reach over his land.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא,
phrases.english: and if you think it is the view of Rabbi Akiva,
why may he trim them?
But he says: one who sells, sells generously!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the textual proof for רבא's answer in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling 'הגדילו ישפה': if the trees grow, the field owner may trim them

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's generosity may apply only to a pit and cistern
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק rejects רבא's proof. רבי עקיבא's 'sells generously' was said about a pit and cistern, which do not weaken the land. Who says he holds the same about trees?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Say that רבי עקיבא said this about a pit and a cistern, which do not weaken the land. Did you hear him say it about a tree?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק knocks down רבא's proof by limiting where רבי עקיבא's rule applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pit or cistern takes nothing out of the surrounding soil, so a seller can easily be generous about it. A tree's roots and shade do weaken the land, so even רבי עקיבא might not expect the seller to give it extra rights. That means the משנה's 'he may trim' could fit רבי עקיבא too, and רבא's proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / one could say (offering another way to see it)
A pit and a cistern (dug into the ground to hold water)
Did you hear him say so? (you have no source for it)

steps.confusionAlert: רב נחמן בר יצחק is not saying רבי עקיבא disagrees with the משנה. He is saying the משנה might fit רבי עקיבא after all, because his generous-seller rule may not cover trees.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא –
phrases.english: He said to him: Say that Rabbi Akiva said this
phrases.notes: This is רב נחמן בר יצחק answering רבא.

phrases.english: regarding a pit and a cistern,
which do not weaken the land;
regarding a tree, did you hear him say it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵימוֹר דְּאָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from 'ישפה' by limiting רבי עקיבא's rule to things that do not harm the land.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's proof that the משנה cannot follow רבי עקיבא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumes רבי עקיבא's generous-seller rule covers trees, but he may have said it only about a pit and cistern, which do not weaken the land.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא agrees that leaning branches may be cut
steps.stepSummary: Support for the rejection: רבי עקיבא himself agrees that a tree leaning into a neighbor's field may be cut back up to the height of an ox-goad over a plow. So trimming fits his view too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't רבי עקיבא agree about a tree leaning into another person's field, that the field owner cuts it back as high as an ox-goad held over a plow?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק continues his rejection of רבא's proof. He points out that רבי עקיבא himself lets a field owner trim branches that get in his way, so trimming fits רבי עקיבא's view too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי עקיבא allows cutting branches that block plowing, then he does not give a tree owner rights that hurt his neighbor. So the משנה's 'he may trim' fits רבי עקיבא, and רבא's proof is gone. That leaves רב נחמן בר יצחק's question from step 4 open again.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that leans or hangs over
An ox-goad, a long stick used to drive oxen while plowing

steps.whatToRemember: רבא tried to prove the משנה isn't like רבי עקיבא from 'he may trim.' The answer: רבי עקיבא's generosity may apply only to things like a pit that don't hurt the land, and he himself lets a neighbor cut branches in his way.

phrases.english: Doesn't Rabbi Akiva agree
about a tree that leans into another person's field,
that he cuts it back the full height of an ox-goad
phrases.notes: 'He' is the owner of the field the branches hang over.

phrases.english: held up over a plow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the rejection in step 7 with a case where רבי עקיבא himself allows trimming a tree.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי עקיבא's generous-seller rule does not stop the field owner from trimming trees
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's agreement in the case of אילן הנוטה לתוך שדה חבירו, which is cut back the height of an ox-goad over a plow

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי חייא בר אבא's ruling: the buyer of three trees acquires the ground under them, between them, and space outside them for a fig-picker and his basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבי חייא בר אבא: The buyer has acquired the ground under the trees and between them, and outside them as much as a fig-picker and his basket need.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same as the ruling quoted back in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 gave the end of a ruling that the buyer gets space for a fig-picker and his basket. Here a ברייתא says exactly that and adds the ground under and between the trees. This gives a ברייתא backing to רבי חייא בר אבא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught that supports him

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives the practical rule for buying three trees: the buyer owns the ground under and between them, plus working space around them for picking.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in line with Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
phrases.notes: This backs up the ruling we saw at the very start, about space for the fig-picker and his basket.

phrases.english: This buyer has acquired the ground under them and between them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' are the three trees he bought in someone else's field.

phrases.english: and outside them, as much as a fig-picker and his basket need.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי עקיבא discussion and goes back to the ruling from step 1, bringing a ברייתא to support it.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חייא בר אבא's ruling that the buyer of trees gets space for a fig-picker and his basket
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the buyer acquires the ground under the trees, between them, and outside them as much as a fig-picker and his basket need

steps.title: Who plants the fig-picker's space?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף who may plant the strip around the trees that is reserved for a fig-picker and his basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: That space set aside for a fig-picker and his basket, who gets to plant it?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a practical follow-up question about the space the buyer acquired in Step 9. The question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fig-picker's space is only needed at harvest time. For the rest of the year it could be planted. אביי wants to know whether the tree owner, the field owner, or neither may plant it.

keyTerms.meaning: A fig-picker, the worker who gathers figs from the tree
Who sows them? Who may plant these areas?

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Those [areas for] a fig-picker and his basket,
phrases.notes: This is the space around the trees that the buyer acquired in the ברייתא from Step 9.

phrases.english: who sows them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up about how the space acquired in Step 9 may be used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who has the right to plant the fig-picker's space during the rest of the year.

steps.title: Answer from the outer-garden path
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers from a משנה: the owner of the outer garden may plant the path that the inner garden owner walks through.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned this in a משנה: the outer garden owner may plant the path.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers by pointing to a משנה about two gardens, one inside the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה, the inner garden owner has the right to walk through the outer garden, yet the outer owner may still plant the path. By comparison, the field owner should be allowed to plant the fig-picker's space even though the tree buyer has rights to use it.

keyTerms.meaning: You learned it already, in a משנה
The outer one, meaning the owner of the outer garden

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
The outer one sows the path.
phrases.notes: This is from a משנה about a garden surrounded by someone else's garden. The inner owner has a right to walk through the outer garden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question by comparing it to a משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The field owner may plant it, just as the outer garden owner may plant the path.

steps.title: The comparison fails because the buyer loses out
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the comparison. Planting the path does not hurt the inner owner, but planting around the trees makes the buyer's fallen fruit dirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are these the same? There, the buyer loses nothing. Here, the buyer does lose, because he can say: my fruit is getting dirty.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back. He says the garden-path case is not a fair comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner garden owner can still walk through a planted path, so he is not harmed. The tree buyer is harmed, because fruit that falls into planted crops gets soiled. Since the buyer suffers a real loss, the field owner should not get to plant.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? A phrase that rejects a comparison
The buyer, here the one who bought the trees

phrases.english: He said to him: Are they comparable?!
There, the buyer has no loss,
phrases.notes: "There" is the garden-path case. He can still walk through the path even with plants in it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא – אִית לֵיהּ פְּסֵידָא לְלוֹקֵחַ,
phrases.english: but here, the buyer does have a loss,
since he says to him: The fruits are getting dirty.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם לֵית לֵיהּ פְּסֵידָא לְלוֹקֵחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison רב יוסף made in Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the fig-picker's space and the garden path.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two cases differ in harm: planting does not hurt the path user, but it does hurt the tree buyer.

steps.title: The better match: neither side may plant
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the case matches the last clause of that משנה, which rules that neither owner may plant the path.
steps.simpleTranslation: This case is only similar to the last part of that משנה: neither this one nor that one is allowed to plant it.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב יוסף's comparison, אביי offers a better one from the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last clause of the משנה deals with a case where the inner owner is given a side path, so he is already losing out. There, neither owner may plant. Since the tree buyer also suffers a loss, the same rule applies here: no one plants the fig-picker's space.

keyTerms.meaning: The last clause of a משנה
This one and that one, meaning both parties

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the fig-picker's space may not be planted by anyone, because planting would harm the tree buyer.

phrases.english: This is comparable only to the last clause:
And this one and that one are not permitted to sow it.
phrases.notes: In that clause the inner owner was given a side path, so he already loses out. That is why no one may plant it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected comparison with the correct one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Neither the tree owner nor the field owner may plant the fig-picker's space.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the buyer acquires the ground around the trees, and that neither side may plant the fig-picker's space, just as אביי said.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא in line with אביי: The buyer acquires under the trees, between them, and outside them enough room for a fig-picker and his basket. And neither one may plant it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that states אביי's ruling outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same ברייתא as in Step 9, now quoted with one more line. That line, saying neither side may plant, directly confirms אביי over רב יוסף's first answer.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in line with him: a ברייתא that supports his view
Under them and between them, meaning the trees

steps.whatToRemember: A ברייתא backs אביי: the space for the fig-picker belongs to the tree buyer, but no one may plant it.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Abaye:
This one has acquired under them and between them,
and outside them, the full space of a fig-picker and his basket;
and this one and that one are not permitted to sow it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's conclusion from Step 13 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that neither side may plant the fig-picker's space.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about buying three trees.

steps.title: How far apart may the trees be?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much space must be between the three trees for the buyer to acquire the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much space should there be between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question: what distance between the three trees still makes them one group? This sets up the two opinions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A buyer of three trees acquires the ground around them only if the trees look like one small orchard. If they are too close or too far apart, they do not form that kind of unit. The question asks for the exact range.

keyTerms.meaning: Between them, meaning between the trees

phrases.english: And how much should there be between them?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the three trees a person bought in someone else's field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which strip of ground the buyer gets to how far apart the trees can be.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The allowed distance between the three trees for them to count as one unit.

steps.title: First version: four to eight אמות
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף, in the name of רב יהודה and שמואל, says the trees must be 4 to 8 אמות apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה, in the name of שמואל: from four אמות up to eight.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the first answer: the trees count as a group if they are between 4 and 8 אמות apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under 4 אמות the trees are too crowded to be a real orchard. Over 8 אמות they are too spread out to be one unit. This is one way of reporting what שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: Cubits, a unit of length (about half a meter each)

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
From four cubits up to eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The trees must be 4 to 8 אמות apart.

steps.title: Second version: eight to sixteen אמות
steps.stepSummary: רבא, in the name of רב נחמן and שמואל, says the trees must be 8 to 16 אמות apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן, in the name of שמואל: from eight up to sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: A second report of שמואל's words gives a larger range: 8 to 16 אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions come from שמואל, but they disagree on the numbers. By this view, trees up to 16 אמות apart still form one unit.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not two different rulings by שמואל. It is two different reports of the same ruling, and only one can be correct.

phrases.aramaic: רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Naḥman said that Shmuel said:
From eight up to sixteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of the answer in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The trees must be 8 to 16 אמות apart.

steps.title: אביי tells רב יוסף not to argue with רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: אביי says a משנה supports רב נחמן's version, so רב יוסף should not disagree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Do not argue with רב נחמן, because we learned a משנה that agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges his teacher רב יוסף's version. This line sets up the משנה that he quotes next as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי is not giving a new opinion. He claims an earlier source settles which report of שמואל is right. If the משנה backs 8 to 16, then רב יוסף's 4 to 8 is in trouble.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
Do not disagree with Rav Naḥman,
for we learned a mishna that agrees with him –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's version (step 16) by backing רב נחמן's version (step 17).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's report that the distance is 4 to 8 אמות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה seems to support 8 to 16, so רב יוסף's numbers go against an earlier source.

steps.title: The משנה: a vineyard planted sixteen by sixteen
steps.stepSummary: The משנה in כלאים says rows of vines 16 אמות apart leave room for other seeds to be sown between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One who plants his vineyard with sixteen אמות between rows may bring seeds and sow them there.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי quotes the משנה from מסכת כלאים that he says supports רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually you may not sow other crops in a vineyard (כלאי הכרם). Here the rows are 16 אמות apart and the משנה still calls it "his vineyard"; sowing is allowed only because there is enough open ground between the rows. So planting 16 אמות apart is still a normal planting, which fits רב נחמן's range of up to 16.

phrases.english: As we learned: One who plants his vineyard

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה עַל שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה,
phrases.english: sixteen cubits by sixteen cubits,
phrases.notes: He means the rows of vines are spaced 16 אמות apart.

phrases.english: is permitted to bring seed there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the משנה that אביי promised in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's version: up to 16 אמות still counts as one unit.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in כלאים: at 16 אמות apart, vines count as separate, so sowing is allowed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's story from צלמון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה tells of a farmer in צלמון who planted rows 16 apart and took turns sowing between them, and the חכמים allowed it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: There was a case in צלמון. Someone planted his vineyard sixteen by sixteen אמות. He would bend the branches of two rows to one side and sow the cleared strip. The next year he bent the branches over the strip he had sown and sowed the strip that had been left empty. The case came before the חכמים and they allowed it.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues the same משנה with a real-life story that shows the 16-אמות rule in action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By pushing the vines aside, the farmer kept a clear strip to sow each year, switching strips every year. The חכמים approved, and the field is still described as a vineyard planted 16 by 16. This strengthens אביי's point that 16 אמות is still a normal planting distance.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: There was an incident in Tzalmon,
with one who planted his vineyard

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה עַל שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה,
phrases.english: sixteen by sixteen cubits,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיָה הוֹפֵךְ שְׂעַר שְׁתֵּי שׁוּרוֹת לְצַד אֶחָד,
phrases.english: and he would turn the branches of two rows to one side,
phrases.notes: Literally "the hair" of the rows, meaning the spreading vine branches.

phrases.english: and sow the cleared land;

phrases.aramaic: לְשָׁנָה אַחֶרֶת הָיָה הוֹפֵךְ אֶת הַשֵּׂעָר
phrases.english: the next year he would turn the branches
to the sown place, and sow the unplanted land;
phrases.notes: The "unplanted land" is the strip that was covered by branches the year before.

phrases.english: and the case came before the Sages and they permitted it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a case that backs up its ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That 16 אמות between rows makes them separate.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים approved the farmer in צלמון who sowed between rows 16 אמות apart.
steps.whatToRemember: Vines planted 16 אמות apart are still called a vineyard. That is why the משנה seems to support רב נחמן's 8-to-16 range.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins his reply: he knows of an actual case
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that he does not know this source, but there was a real case, which the גמרא is about to describe.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I do not know about this, but there was an actual case...
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף starts to defend his version. The sentence continues past this point, so this line sets up the case he is about to tell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף does not argue with the משנה directly. Instead he points to a real case that he believes supports his own numbers. The details of that case continue on the next amud.

phrases.english: He said to him: I do not know,
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף answering אביי.

phrases.english: but there was an incident

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא לָא יָדַעְנָא, אֶלָּא עוֹבָדָא הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב יוסף responds to אביי's challenge from the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a real case instead of explaining the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה about vineyards decides the question in favor of רב נחמן.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף relies on a case he knows (described next) to support his version.
